p.seg: Seventh year, spring, second month, jihai (day 36). [on jihai]
Xianqiu was set on fire.
What does “set on fire” mean?
To burn with firewood.
What does “to burn with firewood” mean?
It means to use fire to launch an attack.
What is implied by “using fire to launch an attack”?
It is an expression of disdain at the first instance of using fire to launch an attack.
What is Xianqiu?
It was a Zhulou settlement.
Why is it not associated with Zhulou? [explicitly linked to]
To present it as the capital. [it is because it treats it as the capital of a state]
Why present it as the capital?
Simply because the ruler was residing there.
Ninth year, spring.
Ji Jiang of Ji was sent to her marital home in the Royal Capital.
If the wording “Queen” of the previous record “gives full realization” to the fact that for the King there is no Exterior,
why does this record designate her as “Ji Jiang of Ji”?
From our Lu perspective we speak in Ji’s voice.
When Ji parents refer to their daughter,
even though she has become Heaven’s Queen,
they would still call her “our Ji Jiang.”
so the wording of the record gives full realization to this!
For the King there is no “Exterior”,
In this case, why is she called “Queen”?
When a bride is in her natal state she is called “daughter”.
Therefore, if we approved of acting as a go between, then the great officer could, on the basis of our approval, use this approval to proceed on to Ji to meet the bride.
The Son of Heaven directed us to act as a go between.
In what way did the completion of his mission depend on us?
The completion of his mission depended on us.
In this case, why does the record say “subsequently”?
A great officer must not initiate a subsequent undertaking.
It indicates an ensuing undertaking.
What does “subsequently” indicate?
In the ritual of marriage, the groom is not designated. [the principal person is not mentioned (as the principal agent)]
Who is the Duke of Zhai?
He was one of the Three Ministerial Dukes of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he not designated as being dispatched?
The Duke of Zhai came.
Subsequently, he went to receive the Queen in Ji. ["welcome" gets the meaning better than the cold "receive"]
Ninth month.
The Marquis of Qi escorted Lady Jiang to Huan.
Why was the record made?
To criticize.
What is criticized by this?
Regional lords crossing state borders to escort a bride,
violate ritual propriety.
Since she had in fact entered the state of Lu,
why not designate her as “the lord’s wife”?
From our Lu perspective we speak in Qi’s voice. [Here DeepSeek has it right: "speaking of Qi"
When Qi parents refer to their daughter,
they would continue to call her “Our Lady Jiang”,
even though she has become the lord’s wife from a neighboring state.
Ninth month.
Ji Liexu came to receive the bride.
Who is Ji Liexu?
He was a great officer of Ji.
Why is he not designated as being “dispatched”?
In marriage rituals no reference is made to the groom.
If so, to whom are references made?
References are made to the father, elder brothers, teachers, and friends.
Then why is there a reference to the groom in the record “The Duke of Song dispatched Gongsun Shou to come to present betrothal gifts”?
The possibility of a ritual pronouncement had been exhausted.
Why had the possibility of a ritual pronouncement been exhausted?
There was no groom’s mother to make the ritual pronouncement.
If so, was there no mother of the Ji’s groom to make the ritual pronouncement?
It is said that there was.
If there was, why is no reference made to this mother?
Mothers’ doings are not communicated.
When a state of the Exterior receives a bride, it is not recorded.
In this case, why is it recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized by this?
The record criticizes the first instance of not welcoming the bride in person.
Did the first instance of not welcoming the bride in person occur on this occasion?
It had occurred before this.
If it had occurred before this, then why is it presented as the first occasion here?
It is simply treated as the first occasion.
Why simply treat it as the first occasion?
It is the first occasion in the Chunqiu.
Why is a daughter of Lu sometimes referred to as “bride”,
sometimes referred to as “wife”,
and sometimes referred to as “the lord’s wife”?
When a daughter is in her natal state she is called “bride”,
when she is on the road, she is called “wife”,
and when she enters her new marital home state she is called “the lord’s wife”.
Third month.
The lord joined by Yifu of Zhulou swore a covenant at Mie.
What does ji (及) mean?
It means yu (與), “to join together”. 【are you sure "together is right here? “get together with" seems better. CH】
Hui (會), ji (及), and ji (暨) all mean yu (與), “to join together”.
So why does the record sometimes say hui (會),
sometimes say ji (及), 【或...或 “sometimes ... at other times" CH】
and sometimes say ji (暨)?
Hui (會) is like zui (最), meaning “to gather together”;
ji (及) is like jiji (汲汲), meaning “pressing”;
and ji (暨) is like jiji (暨暨), meaning “resolutely”,
so ji (及) indicates that we desired the encounter
and ji (暨) indicates that we had no choice. 【" (one) had no choice" "there was no choice" is perhaps just subjectless rather than with ellipsis of subject】
Someone from Jin seized the Marquis of Wei
What does “returned him to” indicate?
and returned him to the Royal Capital.
What does “he was returned to” indicate?
“Returned him to” indicates guilt had already been determined;
“He was returned to” indicates guilt had not yet been determined.
So why, in another record, where the guilt has not yet been determined, could the seizing qualify as an overlord’s punishment?
“Returned him to” (in the present record) indicates
that a person was seized at the behest of the Son of Heaven,
so whether or not he was determined to be guilty,
can be deduced.
“He was returned to” (in the other record)
indicates that a person was not seized at the behest of the Son of Heaven,
so whether or not he was determined to be guilty,
cannot be deduced.
What was the Marquis of Wei’s crime?
He killed Shuwu.
Why was this not recorded?
To respectfully conceal the killing for the sake of Shuwu.
The Chunqiu conceals for the sake of the worthy.
What was worthy about Shuwu?
He yielded the state.
How is it that he yielded the state?
Lord Wen of Jin expelled the Marquis of Wei and installed Shuwu.
If Shuwu had declined to be installed and another had been established in his stead,
he feared that the Marquis of Wei would not be able to return.
Consequently, Shuwu set himself up as lord
and subsequently availed himself of the meeting at Jiantu to manage the return of the Marquis of Wei to his state.
After the Marquis of Wei had been able to return,
“Shuwu usurped my position.”
he declared,
Yuan Xuan disputed this, saying,
“Shuwu is innocent!”
In the end, the Marquis of Wei killed Shuwu
and Yuan Xuan fled and left the state.
This was Marquis of Jin,
why does it designate him as “someone”?
To degrade him.
Why degrade him?
The disaster in Wei was Lord Wen’s creation.
How did Lord Wen precipitate it?
When Lord Wen of Jin expelled the Marquis of Wei to install Shuwu,
he caused an elder and younger brother of another state to suspect one another,
effecting the murder of a maternal younger brother.
It was Lord Wen of Jin who did this!
The Zheng Heir Apparent Hu, resumed his position upon returning home to Zheng.
Why do records sometimes say “assumed his position of rulership upon returning home” and sometimes say “resumed his position of rulership upon returning home”?
Why is he designated “Heir Apparent”?
It indicates the proper succession was restored.
“Resumed his position of rulership upon returning home” indicates the departure was condemnable but the returning home was not condemnable.
“Resumed his position of rulership upon invading”
indicates the departure was not condemnable but the entering was.
“Assumed the position of rulership upon invading”
indicates the departure and the entering were condemnable.
“Assumed the position of rulership upon returning home”
indicates the departure and the entering were not condemnable.
Summer, fourth month. 【: instead of . recommended everywhere, by the way]
Gongzi Bi of Chu assumed the position of rulership upon returning home from Jin to Chu
and assassinated his ruler Qian in Ganxi.
This is a case of assassinating one’s ruler. [the reigning ruler]
Why does the record speak of “assuming the position of rulership upon returning home”? (see Huan 15.5)
Assuming the position of rulership upon returning home was not condemned in relation to the assassination of the established ruler.

Why was assuming the position of rulership upon returning home not condemned in relation to the assassination of the established ruler? [why is it that the returning to his rightful office was not disapproved of on account of the assassination and the establishing himself as a ruler?]
King Ling of Chu was a wayward ruler.
When he built the Platform of Ganxi,
three years passed and still he had yet to complete the project!
Consequently, Gongzi Qiji of Chu coerced Bi into being established as ruler.
Whereupon he issued an order to the Ganxi laborers saying:
“Bi has been established as the ruler.
Anyone who lingers, will not be allowed to return to their fields and hamlets.”
Subsequently, droves of laborers quit and left Ganxi. 【Leave out "subsequently"】
King Ling then hung himself and died.
Gongzi Qiji of Chu assassinated Gongzi Bi.
Bi was already established as the ruler, 【Bi being already established as a ruler】
so why is he designated as “Gongzi” (Lord’s Son)?
He did not intend to usurp rulership.
If he did not intend to usurp rulership,
why is the assassination of the ruler ascribed to him?

It was Bi’s righteous obligation to consider it appropriate to commit himself to death rather than being established as the ruler. 【I think there is no such thing as a "righteous obligation" in English.】
A great officer who kills another great officer is designated as “someone”. 【they are referred to as a person (without any indication of a title)】
In this case, why is Qiji referred to by his personal and lineage name with regard to this assassination? 【in the context of】
To imply that he planned to become the next ruler as a consequence of this assassination. 【this indicates that he was about to, from this point onward, to become the ruler】
Winter, tenth month.
Bo Ji was sent to her marital home in Ji.
Who is Bo Ji?
She was a daughter of Lu.
Why does the record say gui, meaning “to return home”?
When reference is made to a woman being married off, it is called gui, meaning “to be sent to her marital home”.
Summer, fifth month.
The Earl of Zheng vanquished Duan at Yan.
What does “vanquished Duan” indicate?
The Earl of Zheng killed Duan/The Earl of Zheng had Duan killed.
If the Earl of Zheng killed Duan, why does the record say that he vanquished Duan?
To emphasize the Earl of Zheng’s blameworthiness.
Why emphasize the Earl of Zheng’s blameworthiness?
His mother desired to install Duan.
It was the Earl of Zheng himself who killed him.
It would have been better if he simply had not granted her this wish.
Who is Duan?
He was the Earl of Zheng’s younger brother.
Why is he not designated “younger brother”?
To indicate he intended to usurp the state.
Why is the location recorded?
Duan intended to usurp the state.
Why is the location not recorded in the analogous record: “someone from Qi killed Wuzhi”?
The killing occurred inside the Qi state.
If execution occurs inside the state, even in cases of usurpation, the location is not recorded.
In cases where there is no usurpation, even if execution occurs outside the state, the location is also not recorded.
Initial year, spring, the King’s first month.
What is the meaning of “initial year”?
It is the inaugural year of the ruler.
What is the meaning of “spring”?
It is the beginning of the year.
It refers to King Wen.
To whom does “King” refer?
Why does the record first speak of “King” and only after speak of “first month”?
To mark the month as the King’s first month.
So what is the implication of “marking it as the King’s first month”?
To emphasize the Zhou King’s unified rule.
Why does the record not state of the lord that he “acceded to the position of rulership”?
To give full realization to Lord Yin’s intention.
How does the record give full realization to the lord’s intention?
Why did he intend to return it to Huan?
Huan was younger but of nobler rank;
The lord intended to pacify the state and then return it to Huan.
Yin was older but of humbler rank.
However, the difference in their rank was so minute
that none among the people of the capital were aware of the difference.
all of the great officers pushed to install him.
But because Yin was not only older but also worthier,
On that occasion, if Yin had refused to accede to the position of rulership,
he could not have known for sure that Huan’s future establishment as ruler would be guaranteed.
Yin feared that all the great officers were not likely to support such a young ruler.
These are the reasons why, in every respect, Yin’s installment was for the sake of Huan’s future installment as ruler.
If Yin was older and also worthier,
why would it not have been appropriate to install him as ruler?
Sons of the primary wife are installed according to seniority, not according to worthiness;
sons of the other consorts are installed according to noble rank, not according to seniority.
Why was Huan of nobler rank?
His mother was of nobler rank.
Why is the son of nobler rank when his mother is of nobler rank?
the mother follows the nobility of her son.
The son follows the nobility of his mother;
